text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared repository. The heart of CI is the automated build, which compiles the code every time a change is made. After the build, a series of automated tests run to check for errors. This process happens within a CI pipeline, a defined sequence of steps that runs without human intervention. By doing this, developers catch issues early, often within minutes of writing new code. Instead of discovering problems days later during a big merge, CI provides immediate feedback. This saves time, reduces frustration, and keeps the software in a consistently working state.
